questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The thief / entered the house, / in the middle of the night, / quiet.

options.text: in the middle of the night

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'quiet'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverb "quietly" should modify the verb "entered" in this context.
 
• **Quiet **is a **verb** and cannot be used to describe how the thief entered the house.
 
• Hence, the erroneous part of the sentence is *'quiet'* which makes **option 4 **the correct answer. 
 
• The sentence can be corrected by using the adverb **quietly **which means *in a quiet manner.*

**Correct sentence__ - ***The thief / entered the house, / in the middle of the night, / **quietly**.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Reconnoitre
questions.solution:

• Reconnoitre is a verb which means to make a military observation of (a region).

 
 
• Example - *They **reconnoitred **the beach some weeks before the landing.*
 
 
 
• The meaning of the given options are as follows - 
 
 
• Glance - take a brief or hurried look. - Shiela **glanced **at the clock.*
 
• Disclaim - refuse to acknowledge; deny. -* The school **disclaimed **any responsibility for his death.*
 
• Inspect - look at (someone or something) closely, typically to assess their condition or to discover any shortcomings. - *Customs officers came aboard to **inspect **our documents.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The thieves were caught by the police.

options.text: The police was caught the thieves.
The police were caught the thieves.
The police had caught the thieves.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The police caught the thieves.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.
 
• The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.
 
• The Passive voice in this question is in **Past Indefinite**. Thus, the Active voice will also be in **Past Indefinite**.
 
• In Passive voice, the format is: **Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)**.
 
• Thus, the format of Active voice is: **Subject + V2 + Object**.
 
• For example:
 
 
• The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)
 
• Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)
 
 
 
• The options except option (4) don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The police caught the thieves.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

One expects better behaviour from a senior student.

options.text: Better behaviour was expected from senior student.
As a senior student you need to behave.
Better behaviour is expected from a senior student.
Senior student behaviour is expected better.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****Better behaviour is expected from a senior student.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + infinitive + Object + adjunct (Active voice) **
 
• **Subject (objective case) + to be + past participle + Object (subjective case) **+ adjunct** (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The grocer sells fresh vegetables. (Active voice)*
 
• *Fresh vegetables are sold by the grocer. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘one’.
 
• The **object **of the given subject is ‘behaviour’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• In case of the given sentence, the subject is an unknown entity. Thus it gets removed from the passive sentence. 
 
• **expects **will be changed to **is expected**.
 
• **Adjunct **is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence
 
 
• In the given sentence, *from a senior student *is the **adjunct.**
 
 

Correct sentence - Better behaviour is expected from a senior student.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music.

B. Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.

C. It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world.

D. It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ADCB'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

__
 
• Sentence **A **is the independent sentence and talks about how a giant once heard some lovely music. 
 
• So, sentence **A **is the **first **sentence after rearrangement. It sets the scene for the rest of the passage. 
 
• Sentence **D **describes the music the giant heard as being very sweet and explains what the giant thought about the music. Hence, **D follows A.__**
 
• Sentence **C **which describes how the music came from a bird and why the giant thought differently should come after sentence** D**, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence **B** is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding the next occurrences observed by the giant. 
 
• Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 1 i.e. ADCB.**

** So, the correct paragraph is : *****A.** One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music. **D.** It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by. **C. **It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world. **B.** Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.*

• **beside - **We use beside to mean "close to" or "next to." - *The shop is **beside **the temple.*

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'heard'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look into the usage of the given options - 
 
 
• prejudiced - having or showing a dislike or distrust that is derived from prejudice; bigoted.
 
• neglected - suffering a lack of proper care.
 
• heard - perceive with the ear the sound made by (someone or something).
 
• removed - take (something) away or off from the position occupied.
 
 
 
• From the above it is clear that heard is the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
 
• Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

Complete passage__ - *The contract (1) __between__ the author and the reader is a game. And the game is one of the greatest inventions (2) __of__ Western civilisation: the game of telling stories, inventing characters and creating the (3) __imaginary__ paradise of the individual, from whence no one can be expelled (4) __because__, in a novel, no one owns the truth and everyone has the right to be (5) __heard__ and understood.*
